projects.name: coding-agent-from-scratch
projects.subtitle: A terminal coding agent, built from first principles
projects.summary: A command-line coding assistant built without an agent framework. Repository maps, sandbox escape tests and A/A controls put each design decision to the test.
highlights: A native tool-calling ReAct loop with seven tools. SEARCH/REPLACE editing uses a four-tier matching chain to handle whitespace and partial-line drift. Shell commands run inside macOS Seatbelt, with boundaries verified by escape tests. About 1,140 lines of core code under 60 tests, 12 of them on sandbox policy.

The repository map uses tree-sitter definitions and references to build a file graph, then personalized PageRank to rank context for the task. Constraining edges by actual Python imports raised edge precision from 32% to 100% without dropping a true edge. IDF-weighted seeds addressed query understanding.

On a 112-file repository, the map reduced task steps by 21% and input tokens by 33%. Read that next to its noise: an A/A arm put the input-token noise floor at about 26%, so the 33% sits only just above it, and at n=1 the figure was +6%. It describes that controlled experiment, not a guarantee.

The evaluation harness runs an A/A arm by default, putting effects beside their noise floor; this led me to retract an earlier claim. In this architecture, output caps made history compression unnecessary. Sub-agent isolation used 71% more total tokens (184,130 delegated against 107,466 not delegated, a 1.71x ratio) for 22% less main-loop context, with no gain in completion or correctness. Raw traces are committed.

metrics.label: More tokens when delegating
metrics.qualifier: For 22% less main-loop context, no gain

projects.name: lumen
projects.subtitle: Autonomous mathematics research agent — billing and budget subsystem
projects.role: Team project · owned the billing and budget subsystem
projects.summary: An agent that does mathematics research on its own: a lead splits the work among readers, real computation runs in a sandbox, and every step and its cost streams live and can be steered. I owned the layer that makes that spending accountable.
highlights: The project (team-built): readers search arXiv, OpenAlex and the OEIS in parallel and run real computation in a network-less Docker sandbox with Python (NumPy, SymPy, NetworkX, Matplotlib). Every step and its cost streams to the browser live, and you can message a running task, stop it, or edit your last message and run it again.

I owned the server-side billing module: a wallet ledger with atomic per-task expenses, an ordered budget responsibility chain, a default per-account cap with an approval flow, Stripe test-mode top-ups with receipts, authenticated encryption for user-supplied API keys, and staff account administration with actor checks.

Why that layer matters: this agent calls models and runs computation on its own, which means it spends money on its own. A budget has to be able to refuse an action before it runs, refusals have to leave a trail, approvals have to be attributable, and ledger ownership has to survive account deletion.

Every feature commit ships with its own test file — ledger, budget chain, Stripe, key encryption, approval lifecycle and HTTP boundaries. Keeping that discipline inside a codebase someone else leads is what I took away from this project.

Attribution: the project is led by ziyangliu-666 (170 commits); I am the second contributor with 32 of about 227. Parallel scheduling, literature search and sandboxed execution were other members’ work.

projects.name: bodycraft-oss
projects.subtitle: Multi-path retrieval with measured scoring weights
projects.summary: An open-source re-implementation of the five-path retrieval I built at SAIC, with per-path score breakdowns and weights treated as a measurable ranking problem rather than a matter of taste. Design complete, implementation in progress.
highlights: Runs filename and path, section title, SQLite FTS5, dense-vector and entity-graph retrieval in parallel. Results merge per file with per-path scores exposed.
Moves hard-coded scoring parameters into hot-reloadable configuration, so weights can be searched against a labelled evaluation set instead of being fixed in code.
Index schemas, configuration and ranking metrics (NDCG, MRR, Hit@K) are covered by 17 tests. The pipeline runs offline without an API key.

The README labels every claim [design] or [built]: no benchmark has run, so this repository reports no measured ranking results. The weight-search method and measured figures from the internal SAIC version belong to that team and are out of scope here.

projects.name: Internal spreadsheet Q&A platform
projects.subtitle: Conversational spreadsheet analysis
projects.role: Backend contributor · patent co-inventor — SAIC team platform
projects.summary: Turns natural-language questions over uploaded spreadsheets into verified SQL, result tables and charts. Structured plans, whitelisted actions and role-based isolation define what the system can execute.
highlights: A team platform: FastAPI and SQLAlchemy backend on MySQL, Redis, MinIO and Qwen, with a React front end streaming over SSE. Rolled out to 20+ internal pilot users, whose trial feedback estimated about two hours of manual work saved per person per day.
My scope was the storage and async layer: uploads to MinIO with table metadata in MySQL, a Redis-backed task queue with scheduler and worker processes for ingestion, and Redis caching.

Co-designed and helped build the Planner–Executor refactor. The planner emits only a structured plan — intent, target fields, actions, constraints and failure policy; the executor runs whitelisted actions over a read-only SQL layer with table-, field- and role-level whitelists. The second phase of the refactor was led by other team members.

Co-authored the invention disclosure as one of the inventors, filed June 2026 and under examination; the method gates execution on a pre-execution score in which access compliance is a hard gate. The core was later rebuilt as a native tool inside an open-source agent runtime, exposing only a controlled clarify / result_table / result_chart protocol.
